title: Hiring Freeze & Headcount Ramp‑Down: Operational Playbook
author: Asha Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the operational steps, owner responsibilities, communication templates, and downstream people‑ops and manager actions when Redwood invokes a hiring freeze or a planned headcount ramp‑down. It is intended to minimize business disruption, protect candidate and employee experience, and ensure legal/compliance alignment.

Scope: Applies to all full‑time, contractor, and contingent hiring processes globally; covers paused offers, paused new‑hire onboarding, redeployment, budget handling, and manager obligations. Does not replace any legally required layoff or redundancy processes; those are handled by the employment law & finance playbooks.

When to use this playbook (Triggers)

- Executive mandate issuing a hiring freeze for organization/BU/role family.
- Finance request to reduce headcount run‑rate by X% within specified window.
- Regulatory or M&A-related temporary pause on new hires.

Decision authority and owners

1. Final approver: VP People Ops or Chief People Officer (CPO).
2. Operational lead: Head of People Operations (owner for execution).
3. Finance representative: Director of Finance Planning (responsible for headcount reforecast).
4. Legal & Compliance: General Counsel (advises on offer communications and any rescinds).
5. Communications: Internal Comms partner (company wide messages).

High-level principles

- Transparency: Clear, timely communication to internal and external stakeholders.
- Fairness: Consistent treatment across similar roles and geographies.
- Candidate protection: Respectful and legally compliant handling of offers and interviews.
- Reuse before reduce: Prioritize redeployment and internal mobility before external termination.

Operational checklist: People Ops (pre‑freeze readiness)

1. Freeze playbook kit ready: templates, FAQ, comms channels, spreadsheet templates (headcount tracker).
2. Identify scope: BU/role families/regions impacted; publish a one‑line scope summary.
3. Create an audit of active requisitions, offers in flight, and candidates at each pipeline stage.
4. Pause automation: disable auto-approve workflows in ATS for new roles; set tagging on active candidates (e.g., HF-2025).

Manager checklist (immediate actions when freeze announced)

1. Stop all new interview bookings unless explicitly exempted.
2. For offers in negotiation: notify People Ops within 24 hours using the OffersInFlight form.
3. Communicate to immediate team within 48 hours using manager template (see below).
4. Review upcoming 30/60/90 plans for new hires and adjust priorities.

Handling candidate pipelines

- Candidates with signed offers: follow legal/comply guidance — generally honored unless extraordinary circumstances; if rescind needed, escalate to Legal and Finance.
- Offers verbally extended but unsigned: default to pausing; People Ops drafts holding correspondence with an estimated timeline.
- Candidates in late‑stage onsites: People Ops and hiring manager must decide within 3 business days to either continue (if exempt) or pause and present options (deferral, internal referral).

Offer rescind & pause protocols

1. Offer rescind is last resort. Only HR + Legal + Finance may approve.
2. If rescind is approved: prepare written notice with rescind rationale, any severance/fee offers (if applicable), and recruiter outreach script.

Template: Candidate hold email (use People Ops ticketing to send)

Subject: Update on your application with Redwood Inference

Hi [Candidate],

Thank you for your continued interest in Redwood Inference. We want to share a short update: due to a company-wide hiring pause announced on [date], we are temporarily pausing hiring for the [role]. We remain impressed by your background and will hold your materials on file. If circumstances change, we will reach out with next steps. You do not need to take any action at this time.

We appreciate your patience.

Best,
[Recruiter Name] on behalf of Redwood People Ops

New hire onboarding & in‑flight offers

- Start dates for already-accepted offers: People Ops to confirm each case. Prefer to honor start dates where possible. If delay required, provide at least 10 business days' notice and an updated onboarding schedule.
- Onboarding tasks: People Ops to place new hires into an onboarding ‘deferred’ queue in HRIS; managers to receive an alternate 30/60/90 plan template.

Redeployment & internal mobility

- Priority redeployment path: Managers with freezes must review at-risk roles and identify internal candidates who can be redeployed.
- Internal mobility fair: People Ops coordinates a 10-day redeployment window where hiring approvals for internal transfers can be expedited.

Compensation and benefits considerations

- Compensation holds: Any comp changes tied to headcount savings must be approved by VP People & Finance and documented.
- Contractor conversion: Pause external contractor-to-FTE conversions unless approved by Finance.

Performance, feedback, and calibration during freeze

- Ongoing performance cycles continue as scheduled. Managers must document promotion/raise decisions but may defer implementation dates if tied to headcount releases.
- For employees taking on additional responsibilities due to hiring freeze, managers should log role stretch assignments and propose temporary recognition (spot bonuses or time‑based allowances), subject to budget approval.

Communication plan (timeline and audiences)

1. Executive announcement (Day 0): All‑company email from CEO with People Ops FAQ attached.
2. Manager briefing (Day 0–1): Live manager town hall + manager kit (talking points, email templates).
3. Candidates & external facing (Day 1–3): People Ops sends holding communications to active pipeline.
4. Ongoing updates (weekly until lifted): Publish a short status update on Confluence and via #people-ops Slack channel.

Escalation matrix and SLAs

- People Ops to respond to manager cases within 24 business hours for offers in flight.
- Legal review for any offer rescind: 48 hours SLA.
- Finance reforecast delivery: 5 business days.

Owner matrix (roles & responsibilities)

| Activity | Primary Owner | Secondary | SLA |
|---------|---------------|-----------|-----|
| Freeze decision & public announcement | CPO | CFO | Day 0 |
| Offer in-flight triage | People Ops Lead | Recruiting Manager | 24 hrs |
| Legal approval (rescinds) | GC | People Ops | 48 hrs |
| Budget reforecast | Finance Dir | People Ops | 5 business days |

Legal & compliance notes

- Local labor law: Follow local employment law for rescinds or delayed start dates; consult Legal for jurisdictional variations.
- Documentation: Maintain an audit trail of all candidate communications for 7 years in case of disputes.

Manager scripts & templates (examples)

Manager -> Team brief (short):
Hi team — leadership has announced a temporary hiring pause that affects new roles and some open reqs. This does not change our current priorities. We will: 1) pause scheduling new interviews; 2) keep offers that are signed; 3) work with People Ops on redeployment options. I’ll follow up with role-specific impacts by [date].

Manager -> Candidate (phone script):
- Thank you for your patience. I want to be transparent: we are under a temporary hiring pause. We value your candidacy; we expect to have more visibility in X weeks. Are you open to a short deferral conversation?

Operational tools & tagging

- ATS tagging: Add tag HF-2025 + status (hold/rescind/continue).
- HRIS queue: Create ‘Deferred Onboarding’ status.
- Reporting: People Ops publishes weekly headcount dashboard (affected reqs, offers in flight, start date changes).

Example timeline scenarios

Scenario A: Short pause (2–6 weeks) — Hold candidates, honor signed offers, defer starts with 10 business days' notice.
Scenario B: Extended pause (6–26 weeks) — Prioritize internal redeployments, review contingent labor, reassess compensation levers.
Scenario C: Ramp‑down (intent to permanently reduce run rate) — Follow redundancy/layoff legal playbook and finance headcount reduction policies.

Post‑freeze wrap up

- Postmortem: People Ops to convene stakeholders within 10 business days of lift to review impacts, pipeline loss, candidate feedback, manager burden, and cost/benefit outcomes.
- Reinstatement checklist: Approvals, ATS unpause, reopen role prioritization, communications plan for re-hiring.

Metrics & reporting (what we track)

- Offers paused vs rescinded (count).
- Time-to-hire impact after lift (delta vs baseline).
- Internal redeployments completed.
- Candidate NPS / recruiter outreach satisfaction.

Appendices

A. Communications templates (full versions are stored in People Ops templates library).
B. Sample JIRA/Asana tags and workflows for tracking deferred onboardings.
C. Quick checklist for managers (1‑page PDF).

Contact & escalation

If you have immediate questions about a specific offer or candidate, open a ticket in People Ops (queue: HiringFreeze) or email people-ops@redwood.ai. For legal/contractual questions, contact legal@redwood.ai.
